EC1: 1. History or presence of allergy [AND] to the study drugs or their components or drugs of their class, or a history of drug or other allergy that, in the opinion of the physician responsible, contraindicates their participation
EC2: 2. Any finding of the medical examination (including blood pressure, pulse rate and electrocardiogram) deviating from normal and of clinical relevance
EC3: 3. History or diagnosis of any significant medical conditions: Including but not limited to gastrointestinal [OR], hepatic [OR], renal [OR], respiratory [OR], cardiovascular [OR], metabolic [OR], immunologic [OR], hematological [OR], psychiatric [OR], neurological [OR], oncological [OR] or hormonal disorders
EC4: 4. Known elevated liver enzymes in past clinical trials with any compound (experimental or marketed)
EC5: 5. Clinically relevant laboratory abnormalities (e.g. Hgb [OR]<11g/dL, Hct [OR]<30g/dL, total cholesterol [OR] >240mg/dL, triglycerides [OR] >500mg/dL, fasting glucose [OR] >130mg/dL, liver function tests [OR] >2.5x upper limit of normal, baseline international normalized ratio >1.2)
EC6: 6. History of evidence of clinically significant hepatic [OR], cardiac [OR], pulmonary [OR], endocrine [OR], immunological [OR], gastrointestinal [OR], hematological [OR], vascular [OR] or collagen disease
EC7: 7. History of alcohol abuse [OR] or use of any illicit drugs
EC8: 8. Unable to abstain from more than one beer or alcohol equivalent per day for the duration of the study
EC9: 9. Use of tobacco products [OR] and/or history of smoking within the past 2 months
EC11: 11. Sexually active women of childbearing age who do [NOT] not use an acceptable barrier method of birth control
EC12: 12. Hypersensitivity to caffeine [OR], warfarin [OR], vitamin K [OR], omeprazole [OR], dextromethorphan [OR], midazolam [OR], tipranavir [OR], ritonavir or their excipients
EC13: 13. Concomitant treatment with other experimental compounds
EC14: 14. Concomitant administration of any prescription or over the counter medications known to alter P450 enzyme [OR] or P-gp activity
EC15: 15. Concomitant administration of any prescription or over the counter medications known to be highly dependent on [OR] P450 or P-gp for clearance for which elevated plasma concentrations [AND] are known to be associated with serious toxicity
EC16: 16. Concomitant administration of any food product known to alter P450 enzyme [OR] or P-gp activity such as grapefruit juice [OR], Seville oranges
EC17: 17. Concomitant administration of any drug that could affect bleeding (e.g., aspirin [OR], clopidogrel [OR], ticlopidine [OR], warfarin [OR], heparin [OR], low-molecular weight heparin)
EC18: 18. Concomitant administration of oral contraceptives (may be included with 7-day washout period)
EC19: 19. Concomitant administration of any herbal medications
EC22: 22. Clinically unacceptable result at the screening physical examination [AND]
EC23: 23. Use of investigational medications within 30 days before study entry
